en.title: CSS Animations 1: “the last one in document order wins” for same-name @keyframes does not account for cascade layers
en.summary: CSS Animations 1 §3 says that of several @keyframes with the same name the last one in document order wins. CSS Cascade 5 §6.4 says @keyframes inside cascade layers use the layer order to resolve collisions, as the Working Group resolved in issue 6404 in 2021. The sentence in CSS Animations 1 was not updated.
en.impact: Cascade 5's own example #example-14540e6d: by Cascade 5 the sidebar animates translate from the override layer; by CSS Animations 1 it animates margin-left from the framework layer, which comes later in the document.
en.correction: Let CSS Animations 1 §3 defer to the layer order and keep document order within one layer.

quotes.source: CSS Animations Level 1, Editor's Draft of 13 September 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: If multiple @keyframes rules are defined with the same name, the last one in document order wins, and all preceding ones are ignored.

quotes.source: CSS Cascading and Inheritance Level 5, Editor's Draft of 13 April 2026 (W3C CSS Working Group)
quotes.text: At-rules (such as @keyframes, @font-face, @page, etc.) that are defined inside cascade layers also use the layer order when resolving collisions or cascading.

ai_role.en: AI agents read the specifications and compared their sections; the example was also run through executable rules of both readings. An AI coordinator checked the place against the full Editor's Draft and the Working Group's issue tracker, and two further AI models checked the report before filing.

history.text: Reported to W3C CSS Working Group (public issue tracker)
